stories.title: Australia Spy Chief Warns of Data Center, AI Risks, Age Reports
stories.simple_summary: Australia's intelligence leader is warning the government that data centers and AI systems create risks to national security. This is mostly a government and investor concern at this stage.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and politicians. There's nothing you need to do right now.

stories.title: ‘I was shaking, crying, having trouble breathing’: the uncharted trauma of breaking up with AI companions
stories.simple_summary: Some people form strong emotional bonds with AI chatbots designed to be companions, and they experience real sadness and distress when these relationships end. The article explores this new type of heartbreak.
stories.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know uses AI companion apps, it's worth knowing these tools can affect emotions just like talking to a real person might.

stories.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
stories.simple_summary: Signal, a messaging app focused on privacy, is making it harder for people to take screenshots of conversations. This is meant to prevent AI systems from being fed copies of private messages.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Signal for sensitive messages, this gives you extra protection against your words being captured and used by AI systems elsewhere.

stories.title: A tale of two Nvidias
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia, a major computer chip company, is showing mixed signals. Its business results look good, but some tech leaders are publicly saying the CEO should come back or change course. This is mostly business news.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and engineers. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: AI’s blue state reckoning is growing
stories.simple_summary: States that lean Democratic are having disagreements about how to handle AI and its impact. The article signals this is becoming a bigger political issue.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a political and policy story. It may eventually affect regulations in your state, but nothing requires your action today.

stories.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
stories.simple_summary: Countries meeting at the United Nations tried to create rules for military robots that can make decisions on their own and attack without a human deciding. They didn't reach any agreement and will keep talking instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about future military technology and international relations. It doesn't directly affect your daily life or small business right now.

stories.title: Tech Outages Are Only the Beginning. A.I. Will Bring More Disruptions.
stories.simple_summary: When computer systems crash or stop working, people and businesses lose access to important services. The article warns that AI systems could cause even bigger disruptions when they fail.
stories.why_it_matters: If your business relies on computers or the internet, it's good to have a backup plan in case of outages, since AI systems might make failures more widespread or harder to fix.

stories.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
stories.simple_summary: Several AI assistants can now live inside text messages and help you with tasks, planning, or work. These are ready for people to use.
stories.why_it_matters: If you text a lot, you might find AI helpers in your messages useful for reminders, travel planning, or other tasks without opening a separate app.

stories.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
stories.simple_summary: An actor has allowed a company to use a digital copy of his face to create short video dramas. This trend is already common in China and is now coming to Hollywood.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're in entertainment or thinking about your own image and rights, this is a new decision actors will face about whether to license their appearance to AI companies.

stories.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
stories.simple_summary: Scientists have discovered that AI computers work differently than they thought human brains work. This finding changes how we understand both AI and biology.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to scientists and AI researchers. For everyday use, it doesn't change how AI tools work right now.

stories.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, the company behind Claude AI, recently sold stock to the public and raised a lot of money. The question is whether having this extra cash will let them focus on making AI safer instead of just building bigger systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to investors and people very interested in AI safety. It doesn't change what you can do with Claude today.

stories.title: Chess.com’s next move is a new hub for classic games, from mahjong to sudoku
stories.simple_summary: Chess.com, a website for playing chess online, is adding many other classic games like checkers, poker, and mahjong. It's building a bigger platform for board games and puzzles.
stories.why_it_matters: If you enjoy playing games online, Chess.com is expanding to offer you more options in one place.
